newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges Gulf states to normalise ties - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges Gulf states to normalise ties - paper.

text.p: Iraq's ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra on Monday urged its Gulf neighbours to normalise ties with Baghdad, saying such a gesture would be useful for both sides.
"The resumption of relations between Iraq and Arab Gulf states to its previous levels would bring positive results for Iraq as well as for these Arab Gulf states," the paper said.

Iraq's relations with Arab Gulf states have been strained since Baghdad's invasion of Kuwait in 1990. Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, United Arab Emirates and Oman fought alongside the U.S-led multinational force that evicted Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991.
Oman and Qatar have since improved ties with Baghdad but others like Saudi Arabia and Kuwait reject direct dealings with Iraq.
Iraq has made similar overtures in the past asking Gulf states, including Kuwait, to turn a new page and renew relations with Baghdad.
